A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSBO reduction framework. The complete documents, including Appendices A–E, equations, tables and figures, are readable, and relocated or renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original MNIST hyperparameter-optimization experiments and simulated traffic inverse-optimization results in Section 5, Figures 1–2 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains both sets of original experimental results, with inverse optimization presented before hyperparameter optimization.

M1.justification: The linear basis parameterization, joint-sampling reduction and use of existing SBO solvers remain unchanged. Reorganizing the Chebyshev guarantees does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate temperature-dependent MNIST data cleaning with 30% label corruption and capacity estimation on the same synthetic two-edge traffic network. Continuous temperatures were already specified in v2 Appendix A; v3's expanded description adds no task coverage.

E2.justification: Both experiments retain the same stocBiO comparators and basis variants. DL-SGD and RT-MLMC remain explicitly omitted; BSA, TTSA and HOAG are mentioned without being evaluated in either version.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains the same splits, sampling distributions, batch size, hyperparameter searches and evaluation procedures. These include 19,000/1,000 MNIST training/validation images, 1,000/1,000 inverse-optimization training/test samples and averaging over the final 10% of epochs.

E4.justification: The same analyses of basis choice, basis size, lower-level approximation error and parameter-estimation error are retained. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report 20 randomized trials for MNIST and 50 runs for inverse optimization, with 95% confidence intervals assuming normally distributed errors for the latter. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The inverse-optimization summary changes stocBiO's remaining disadvantage from failing to match training loss to failing to match lower-level error, and recasts the N=10/N=100 comparisons as thresholds. This is a limited revision of the stated finding; all five plotted panels are identical.

T1.justification: Appendix E corrects the analyticity lemma's premise from v2's density condition to v3's analyticity condition (Lemma E.1 to E.3). The conditioning proposition also changes from invoking all of Assumption 4.6 to condition (c.1) alone. The principal guarantees and substantive derivations remain intact.

C1.justification: Both claim a joint-sampling CSBO-to-SBO reduction, hypergradient accuracy, near-optimal complexity using suitable bases, and empirical efficiency benefits. v3 foregrounds general basis criteria already supported by v2 Theorem 4.4, without adding a distinct core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds applicability discussion involving finite-task meta-learning, personalized federated learning and bounded context distributions. Section 4.2 removes the explicit qualification that rescaling cannot compensate for insufficient expressiveness or poor conditioning. Existing empirical mechanism explanations and adaptive-basis future work remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A removes the explicit step-size restriction beta_0 <= 1/Lg,1 and its comparison with beta_0 = 1/(4mu) when explaining omitted DL-SGD/RT-MLMC methods. Hardware, runtime, data-generation instructions and settings for the evaluated methods are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 48 cited works are retained. Section 2 revises its discussion of prior CSBO work to emphasize solving fresh lower-level problems without warm starts, while the hyperparameter section makes its continuous-temperature positioning relative to prior finite-temperature formulations more explicit.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary and conclusion are edited, and Section 4.3 consolidates the Chebyshev assumptions and theorem. Experiment subsections are reversed in Section 5 and Appendix A; definitions and normalization discussion move to Appendix E. The overall structure and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The inverse-optimization figure changes from Figure 2 to Figure 1, and the MNIST figure changes from Figure 1 to Figure 2, with corresponding relocation. Plot panels, axes, legends and appendix tables are retained; surrounding text and equation placement change.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the relationship between general basis criteria and the Chebyshev example, corrects the analyticity premise, and aligns the inverse-optimization summary with the lower-level-error plot. These provide modest clarity and accuracy gains. The shorter baseline-omission explanation loses some technical detail, while the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
